title: The Claude API: Your First Requests

questions.prompt: Which endpoint do all Claude API requests go through?

options.text: A different endpoint for every feature

questions.explanation: Everything goes through the Messages API. Tools, structured output, and thinking are features of that one request.

questions.prompt: Match each stop_reason to its meaning.

pairs.right: Hit the output cap; the reply is cut off

questions.explanation: Always check stop_reason before trusting content: truncation, tool calls, and refusals each need different handling.

questions.prompt: Because the Messages API is ____, you must resend the whole conversation to continue it.
questions.explanation: The server remembers nothing between requests; continuity comes from the messages list you send.

questions.prompt: Which are good practices for your first integration? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the API key in an environment variable
Loop over content blocks and check each block's type
Hard-code the key so teammates can run the script

questions.explanation: Keys belong in the environment, content is a list of typed blocks (a thinking block may come first), and streaming avoids timeouts on long outputs.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to make your first API call.

items.text: Call messages.create with a model, max_tokens, and messages
Create an API key in the Claude Console
Read the content blocks, stop_reason, and usage
Store the key in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and install the SDK

questions.explanation: Get a key, store it in the environment and install the SDK, send the request, then read the structured response.

questions.prompt: A request to Opus 5.5 uses 2,000 input and 500 output tokens. At $4/$20 per million tokens, what does it cost?
